function.mechanism: Provides orange-red coloration via light absorption by its conjugated carotenoid/apocarotenoid polyene chain.
common_food_categories: Solid and semisolid foods (U.S. general authorization with limits)
Liquid foods (U.S. general authorization with limits)

adi.basis: EFSA 2014 reconsideration; temporary 0.05 mg/kg bw/day in 2012 was revised after additional data and refined exposure assessment.

efsa.key_finding: At current reported use and use levels, beta-apo-8'-carotenal (E160e) did not raise a safety concern; refined exposure estimates were below the revised ADI.

adi.basis: JECFA 2019 (meeting 87) established ADI 0-0.3 mg/kg bw based on a 13-week rat NOAEL of 30 mg/kg bw/day and UF 100.

concerns.summary: In vitro studies reported DNA damage-related signals with beta-apo-8'-carotenal or carotenoid breakdown products in human cell models (A549 and ARPE-19) under experimental conditions.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2014 concluded no safety concern at current reported use levels with ADI 0.3 mg/kg bw/day.
JECFA 2019 set ADI 0-0.3 mg/kg bw/day for beta-apo-8'-carotenal.
U.S. 21 CFR 73.90 authorizes use with explicit concentration limits.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2012 temporary-ADI scenario indicated potential exceedance in children, but EFSA 2014 refined exposure estimates (children up to 0.20 mg/kg bw/day high percentile) were below the revised ADI of 0.3 mg/kg bw/day.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory bodies (EFSA, JECFA, U.S. CFR) permit use with defined ADI/use limits and no current conclusion of unacceptable risk at authorized exposures; mechanistic in vitro signals justify caution but do not currently outweigh the regulatory toxicology conclusions.
key_factors: EFSA ADI 0.3 mg/kg bw/day and 2014 no-safety-concern conclusion at reported use levels
21 CFR 73.90 use restrictions (15 mg/lb solids or semisolids; 15 mg/pint liquids)
No IARC monograph classification identified for this agent
In vitro DNA-damage/mechanistic signals in selected cell systems
